answer: Harbor-Interval Admission. An identity joins only if its first N actions arrive in bursts whose inter-arrival gaps match a human session shape (bursty starts, decaying tail). Agents flagging steady machine cadence wait out a quarantine. Onyx labels each delayed identity, so an attacker must rent real humans or idle synthetic accounts through the full decay window before any action counts. Ocean-wide botnets still pay the calendar delay per identity, multiplying campaign setup time linearly.
